https://t.co/VsRxsKY3Hf
  [Quoting @algekalipso: My sense is that just as the phenomenology of a person is a religion that a bunch of cells instante in order to coordinate around replicator goals, the phenomenology of being a God might be quite similar.  You're recruiting bundles of emptiness and applying specific epistemic handicaps in order to create the impression of a singular identity rather than perceiving clearly the hivemind-like nature of the process.  Interacting with a bundle of emptiness larger than oneself during a mystical experience can have one of many different flavors, depending on how the illusion of an enduring self is generated (or not). An advanced meditator friend agrees that the quality of interacting with a God is very different than interacting with a Buddha - the former being a type of experience where a lot of the resources always go to reinforcing the central agentic gestalt and there are insights subtly discouraged. Interacting with a Buddha, as it were, is more akin to interacting with a hivemind where the information that (1) everything is impermanent, (2) the self doesn't really exist as an enduring metaphysical principle, and (3) sensations are dissatisfying (can't ultimately get rid of craving), is holographically encoded in every emergent gestalt. The system coordinates around a more precise and accurate understanding of emptiness than how a self-centered architecture is capable of.  That's what I was trying to point at with the Rainbow Body Collective discussion: you don't need a central vortex or topological defect to organize a mind; even if this method is fairly effective, it comes with epistemological handicaps where realizing the emptiness of self is somehow very difficult or frowned upon.]
